key_insight: FERPO improves continuous-control policies by fitting the actor to a forward-KL target distribution derived from critic values, avoiding direct differentiation of the critic with respect to actions.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more stable on-policy policy-improvement pathway for robotics and control tasks where accurate value estimates do not guarantee reliable action gradients.
method: Derive an entropy- and KL-regularized optimal target action distribution from critic values.
Fit the actor with a forward-KL objective estimated via self-normalized importance sampling from rollout-policy actions.
Use KL regularization to keep importance weights well behaved while encouraging coverage of multiple high-value modes.
evidence_signal: The paper reports competitive performance and sample-efficiency gains on MuJoCo Playground and ManiSkill, plus faster actor updates than REPPO in computational benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance depends on well-behaved importance sampling, so overly weak KL regularization or a target too far from the rollout policy could destabilize training.
